validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: Northern Border Pipeline is a real, major FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transmission pipeline, one of the original 'prebuild' legs of the Alaska Natural Gas Transportation System (ANGTS). FERC issued a conditional certificate to Northern Border Pipeline Company (Docket CP78-124) in December 1977 (confirmed independently by FERC's own ANGTA staff report, ferc.gov/sites/default/files/2020-05/angta.pdf, and the Energy Bar Association's 1982 Report of Committee on Natural Gas Certificate and Authorization, eba-net.org). Construction began 1981, in-service 1982 (UPI wire, Sept 3 1981, contemporaneous; EBA 1982 journal, both independent of the operator). It remains active today: TC Energy's live 2026 operations page (tcenergy.com) and Rextag's current informational-postings page both describe it as an in-service 1,412-mile system. Correctly classified as a large-diameter interstate GAS transmission trunk (not gathering/distribution) throughout. CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any other roster row — Bison (P0158) and Williston Basin (P0281) interconnect with/deliver into Northern Border but are separate certificated systems; no other roster entry names this route. ATTRIBUTION (ownership — the ONE row in this batch's stale-ownership theme found to already be current): TC Energy's own 2026 page states 'TC Energy owns 50 percent of the Northern Border pipeline. The remaining 50 percent is owned by ONEOK Northern Border Pipeline Company Holdings, LLC,' and Rextag's current listing independently states 'Owner: ONEOK Partners (50) / TC Energy Corporation (50).' Both agree exactly with the sheet's current Owner1=TC Energy 50%, Owner2=ONEOK Inc 50% — CONFIRM, do not touch. validity.recommendation: change StartCountryOrArea from 'Canada' to 'United States' — Port of Morgan is the Montana-side (US) border-crossing point; StartState/Province='Montana' is correct and StartCountryOrArea contradicts it
validity.researcher_notes: GEOGRAPHY DEFECT (flagged in the brief as needing settlement): the sheet records StartLocation='Port of Morgan', StartState/Province='Montana', but StartCountryOrArea='Canada' — internally contradictory, since Montana is not in Canada. Two independent sources place the pipeline's own starting point on the US side of the border: offshore-technology/GlobalData states the pipeline 'starts at Montana (the US) and ends in Indiana (the US)'; the Energy Bar Association's 1982 journal states FERC 'granted Northern Border a permit authorizing Northern Border to construct, operate, maintain and connect natural gas transmission facilities at the international boundary near Port of Morgan, Montana' (i.e., the US-side facilities Northern Border Pipeline Company itself owns/operates begin at that Montana border crossing). The FERC ANGTA staff report likewise describes the 'Eastern Leg (Northern Border Pipeline)' as the US segment carrying gas that arrives from Canada, not a Canadian-territory pipeline. GEM's ProjectID P2099 is 'Northern Border Gas Pipeline' (the US FERC-jurisdictional company/system), not the Canadian NGTL supply line feeding it — so StartCountryOrArea should read United States, matching StartState/Province='Montana'. StartLocation, StartState/Province, EndCountryOrArea='United States' are all independently corroborated and correct; only StartCountryOrArea is wrong. EndState/Province='Indiana' and EndLocation='Fort Hayden' are addressed separately below (partial corroboration, lower confidence).

validity.recommendation: no strong recommendation — flag for awareness only; EndLocation/EndState terminus in the far-east portion of the system is the least-corroborated fact on this row
validity.researcher_notes: EndState/Province='Indiana' has only ONE clean independent corroboration found: offshore-technology/GlobalData explicitly states the pipeline 'ends in Indiana (the US)'. TC Energy's own PHMSA public-awareness safety sheets (pipelineawareness.org, 2022) describe the eastern terminus only as the 'Chicago market area' without naming a state, and also give a notably shorter length (1,249 miles) than every other source (all of which — TC Energy's own website, Rextag, ND Legislative Council, GlobalData — agree on 1,412 miles); this may be a stale or mainline-only figure in that particular safety document, an internal TC Energy inconsistency rather than evidence against the sheet. The 1977 ANGTS design (FERC ANGTA staff report) originally certificated the Eastern Leg to run '...to Dwight, Illinois' — the system's terminus has clearly moved/extended east over decades of expansion (Oil & Gas Journal, 1992: acquired a 147-mile Ventura–Harper, Iowa lateral from Natural Gas Pipeline Co. of America, growing the system past its original 823-mile, Illinois-bound design), so an Illinois-only 1977 design terminus does not contradict a present-day Indiana delivery point — it is consistent with known growth. Could not independently verify the specific place name 'Fort Hayden' in any source outside GEM's own wiki page — recommend a researcher check NPMS (www.npms.phmsa.dot.gov) or the TC Energy system map (PDF, mostly raster/image, could not text-extract facility names) to pin the exact current end-point name in a future pass.

validity.researcher_notes: Capacity sources disagree modestly: TC Energy/Northern Border Pipeline Company's own 2022 PHMSA public-awareness disclosure (pipelineawareness.org) states 'a design capacity of 2,374 million cubic feet per day'; Rextag's current informational-postings page states 'System Capacity: 2.5 Bcf/d'; the ND Legislative Council's 2020 report (citing the pipeline company's own customer-meeting materials) also says 'approximately 2.5 billion cubic feet (Bcf) per day.' The sheet's 2,400.00 MMcf/d sits inside this 2,374–2,500 range (roughly a 5% spread, consistent with successive small compression additions/rounding over the pipeline's 40+ year life, not a wrong figure) — per the ref-support convention, a source agreeing within rounding is treated as corroborating, with the discrepancy noted rather than silently passed. Citing the operator's own figure as the primary ref and Rextag as the second, independent figure.
